props.name: hide
props.description: Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the panel, needed when there is no visible heading.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popover is showing. Reflects so page CSS can target it.

props.name: placement
props.description: Preferred side. Flips at the viewport edge rather than clipping, so a `bottom` popover on a trigger near the bottom of the screen renders above.

ai.summary: A floating panel that holds controls, anchored to a trigger.
whenToUse: A button opens a small panel of controls, such as filters or a menu
The panel content is interactive — links, checkboxes, a form
The panel needs to close on Escape and on an outside click
whenNotToUse: The content is only a description of the trigger — use a Tooltip
It must interrupt and demand a decision — use a Dialog
The content is navigation beside the page — use a Drawer
ai.accessibility: `role="dialog"` on the panel, with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded` on the trigger — not `aria-describedby`, which would announce the whole panel as the trigger's description. Focus moves into the panel on open and returns to the trigger on close. Escape and an outside click both dismiss. Unlike a Tooltip, it takes pointer events, because it holds controls. `placement` is logical on the inline axis: `start` and `end` mirror under `dir="rtl"` (ADR-016).
knownLimitations: The panel is rendered by Stencil with real `<slot>` elements — the consumer's children are never relocated, which is what keeps a click on slotted content inside the panel
The flip at the viewport edge is computed for the block axis only; inline-axis placement does not flip
